programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-6 Shandong Mantis Style
programme.desc: The final episode traces the cross-ocean transmission of Shandong Mantis Style. In the mountains of northern Italy, host Kleber visits Dante Basili, a veteran Italian practitioner in his sixties, who recounts travelling to China 36 years ago to learn Mantis Style and returning home to teach Chinese martial arts ever since. Kleber then heads to Shandong to meet Yu Bo and Yu Tao, sons of Mantis Style grandmaster Yu Hai. He witnesses a traditional apprenticeship ceremony and explores the style’s fighting essence: adopting its spirit rather than merely copying its form. The episode shows how Mantis Style has taken root and flourished in different cultural settings. Ultimately, this journey across Europe and Asia suggests that transmission is not only about techniques, but also about dialogue across time and distance, and a shared resonance of spirit between cultures.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: "Foodwise" host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Foodwise: The Herbal Way of Life
programme.desc: 'Medicine tonic is not as good as food tonic' - this Chinese saying is a core principle of Traditional Chinese Medicine. It is believed that the right diet and nourishment can cure and reverse the effects of disease, hence considered an inevitable source of natural health preservation. In this Foodwise episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May explore this ancient concept of medicine food homology as they taste their way through different herbs, chat to experts of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and visit venues that combine conventional principles with modern ideas. Dive deep into the origin of TCM with us as we learn about the harmony between man and nature and its application in modern functional foods!

programme.title: From Stone to Story
programme.desc: China's profound stone carving culture dates back to the Han Dynasty (202 BC – 220 AD) and flourished during the Tang Dynasty (618 – 907 AD), evolving into a distinctive art form and unique cultural practice. Among many places famous for stone carving, Hui’an County—through generations of dedicated artisans—has risen to prominence and earned the esteemed title of "World Capital of Stone Carving," awarded by the World Crafts Council. The county’s skilled stonemasons are celebrated for their ability to transform ordinary pieces of rock into beautiful works of art. This episode shines a spotlight on the intangible cultural heritage of Hui’an stone carving and reveals how it has been influenced by the area’s close proximity to the sea.

programme.title: China Bound: Chongqing
programme.desc: Join us in southwest China's Chongqing, one of the world's biggest cities. From futuristic skylines and cyberpunk streets, to fire-breathing opera, spicy hotpot and kungfu tea, we're diving deep into this megacity the size of Austria.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.3
programme.desc: Inner Mongolia spans China from east to west. Little wonder then, that it's such a land of diversity - epic landscapes of forests, grasslands and deserts, Inner Mongolia has it all!

programme.title: Three Gorges of Chongqing
programme.desc: In this episode, through the new fashion of five-star cruise tour on the Three Gorges, with comfortable and convenient high-end experiences, we take the audience to travel along the river, multi-dimensionally show the most spectacular and beautiful landscape gallery along the Yangtze River, feel the unique charm of canyons, rapids and cultural relics on both banks, and convey the new charm of Yangtze River cultural tourism.

In the mountains of northern Italy, host Kleber visits Dante Basili, a veteran Italian practitioner in his sixties, who recounts travelling to China 36 years ago to learn Mantis Style and returning home to teach Chinese martial arts ever since. Kleber then heads to Shandong to meet Yu Bo and Yu Tao, sons of Mantis Style grandmaster Yu Hai. He witnesses a traditional apprenticeship ceremony and explores the style’s fighting essence: adopting its spirit rather than merely copying its form. The episode shows how Mantis Style has taken root and flourished in different cultural settings. Ultimately, this journey across Europe and Asia suggests that transmission is not only about techniques, but also about dialogue across time and distance, and a shared resonance of spirit between cultures.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: "Foodwise" host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Foodwise: The Herbal Way of Life
programme.desc: 'Medicine tonic is not as good as food tonic' - this Chinese saying is a core principle of Traditional Chinese Medicine. It is believed that the right diet and nourishment can cure and reverse the effects of disease, hence considered an inevitable source of natural health preservation. In this Foodwise episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May explore this ancient concept of medicine food homology as they taste their way through different herbs, chat to experts of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and visit venues that combine conventional principles with modern ideas. Dive deep into the origin of TCM with us as we learn about the harmony between man and nature and its application in modern functional foods!

programme.title: Foodwise: Fuding
programme.desc: Fuding—the land of white tea— is the perfect place for Foodwise hosts Tianran and Hannah to spend the Dragon Boat Festival. Watch them wrap sticky rice dumplings called zongzi, feast on a variety of local snacks and experience the ultimate white tea banquet. From the sea to the mountains, every stop promises a new taste of Fujian.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuyi Mountains
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran and Hannah continue their travels in Fujian province, this time they visit the birthplace of oolong tea. There's plenty to do, from tasting local specialties like rock tea and braised goose to bamboo rafting and hiking Tianyou Peak. To cap it all off, they'll attend a Zhu Xi banquet, named after one of China's greatest Neo-Confucian scholars.

programme.title: Health Explored S01 E09 - Purpose Of Life (Part 2)
programme.desc: We travel to the Japanese island known for having some of the oldest people on Earth. We engage with leading scientists who have identified the "Longevity Gene," offering a glimpse into the genetic factors that contribute to extended lifespans. Beyond genetics, we explore the deeply ingrained cultural practices that sustain long, fulfilling lives in Okinawa. We delve into the importance of "moai," a lifelong social network that supports residents into their golden years, and the principle of "Hara Hachi Bu," which advises eating until you're 80% full while focusing on nourishing foods. But at the core of Okinawan longevity, we find "ikigai"—a profound sense of life purpose. From practicing martial arts to active community participation, we discover that Okinawan seniors maintain a vibrant sense of purpose in various facets of life. Join us on this enlightening journey to learn how the pillars of social support, mindful eating, and a strong sense of ikigai could enhance your own quest for a long and fulfilling life.

programme.desc: Marilia embarks on a captivating journey, capturing the essence of Treasure Island through extraordinary encounters. They film hidden treasures and enchanting allure against stunning backdrops. At Fort DeSoto, Marilia embraces the tranquil beauty of the beach, while Ashley leads them to Boyd Hill National Park for profound conversations beneath a magnificent tree. In Ashley's studio, a tea ceremony symbolizes tranquility and connection, followed by an intimate interview unveiling her artistry. Gulfport Beach becomes a sanctuary for transformative sound healing, and Marilia rides a bike along the boardwalk, capturing the synergy between nature and human activity. Marilia meets Justin, capturing his unique vision and creativity, and encounters Lindy, a captivating sound healer. Dolphin Yoga at CMA merges Marilia's practice with the playful marine world, while Levi guides her through an extraordinary dolphin feeding session. Clearwater Marine Aquarium showcases the dedication of the staff and educates visitors about marine conservation. In Irene's studio, Marilia explores the wellness aspect of Flamenco dance. The journey concludes at Mirror Lake, encapsulating the profound impact of Marilia's experiences through heartfelt testimonials and reflective voice-overs.

programme.title: Departures S03 E02 - Russia - The Bull Of Winter
programme.desc: The guys head northeast into Siberia to reach the coldest inhabited place on earth: the Pole of Cold. Along the way, the word of Scott and Justin’s journey travels and they become local news celebrities. They visit a permanent circus, take part in the Festival of Cold, answer questions at local press conferences and end up judging a quirky beauty contest in Yakutsk. Riding reindeer for the rest of the trek, they camp in the snow before hitting the Pole of Cold.

programme.title: Departures S03 E03 - Sri Lanka
programme.desc: Travelling to Sri Lanka at the tail end of the 25-year civil war, the guys expect to visit a war-torn country, yet discover a different land. From exploring the wonders of Sigiriya, an ancient rock fortress and palace ruin, to visiting Sri Lanka’s indigenous inhabitants, the Veddas tribe, and joining the pilgrimage up Adam’s Peak, the guys experience a beautiful and culturally rich country. They get to Sri Lanka’s capital city, Colombo, just in time to see the Navam Perahera – a spectacular parade made up of thousands of dancers and acrobats, and over a hundred decorated elephants.

programme.title: Departures S03 E04 - Vietnam
programme.desc: Scott and Justin catch up with their high school friend Fran, who is travelling to Vietnam to explore his motherland and family history for the first time. They travel south to north, through the commotion of Ho Chi Minh City and the Mekong River floating markets, and experiencing haunting remnants of the Vietnam war and visiting magical and mysterious temples and caves along the way. Further north, surrounded by the beauty of Halong Bay, the guys realize that spending time with Fran’s family, and seeing the country through his eyes, has given them a fresh perspective on travel.

programme.title: Southern Uncovered with the Lee Brothers S01 E05 - Dallas, TX NB
programme.desc: Matt and Ted Lee land in Dallas for a taste of barbecue that’s smoking the competition before sampling the best of Tex Mex, Mex-Mex and Czech-Mex flavors.

programme.title: Southern Uncovered with the Lee Brothers S01 E06 - New Orleans, LA NB
programme.desc: Matt and Ted Lee head to New Orleans where Creole and Vietnamese flavors merge, modern Israeli food finds a home and a historic cocktail culture gives rise to tasty hangover cures.

programme.title: Descending S01 E04 - The Emerald Sea
programme.desc: Scott brings Ellis and the Descending team home to Canada for some cold-water diving off Vancouver Island. Scott and Ellis make friends with some questionable creatures and then pilot a jet at 80ft below the surface. Above the water, the team is put to work preparing a ship for scuttling.

programme.title: Scottish Islands With Ben Fogle S01 E03 - Northern Outer Hebrides
programme.desc: Ben Fogle returns to Scotland’s sacred Outer Hebrides, exploring Harris and Lewis in a personal journey shaped by spirituality, nature, and community. From ancient rituals to modern faiths, he uncovers transformative island experiences and enduring traditions.

programme.desc: Global traveller, Scott Wilson, returns to Japan to tour around by motorcycle, and experience the country's rich cultural and cuisine offerings found off the typical tourist trail.

programme.title: Travel Man S01 E01 - Barcelona
programme.desc: Richard and actor Kathy Burke do Barcelona in 48 hours, including some far-out cuisine, Cava tasting, a guided tricycle tour and surrealist artist Miro.

programme.title: Travel Man S01 E02 - Istanbul
programme.desc: Richard and comedian Adam Hills embark on a whirlwind visit in Istanbul, including a boat trip, a massage, a very close shave, and some haggling at the Grand Bazaar.

programme.title: Alan Cummings Paradise Homes S01 E03 Highland Hideaways and Caves
programme.desc: On a journey back to his rugged roots of the Scottish Highlands, Alan experiences an extraordinary hidden getaway living in harmony with ancient land, complete with 360 views and golden eagles circling the property. In Sicily, Alan tours an eccentric family home built above a cave, filled with innovative and intricate space-saving details, including a one-of-a-kind bedroom climbing wall!

programme.title: Travel Man S03 E01 - New York - JGO
programme.desc: Richard and comedian Katherine Ryan take a fast and funny trip to New York. Their overflowing schedule includes skyscrapers, roller blades, museums, ferries, show-tunes and cronuts.

programme.title: Race Across The World S02 E09 - Extraordinary Journey, Ordinary People Endure NB
programme.desc: Over 54 days, five pairs of ordinary Brits took on the challenge of a lifetime and attempted to travel, at ground level, the entire length of Latin America: from Mexico City to Ushuaia, Argentina, the most southerly city in the world – with no planes, no credit cards and no smartphones in sight. They came across extreme weather, states of emergency, evacuations, challenging budgets as well as life-changing encounters, incredible acts of generosity and dramatic landscapes. Most of all, they had to survive each other.
